necessary_context.content: A fixed unknown sequence c_1,...,c_n:S→[-C,C] is chosen in advance. At round t choose x_t∈S, then observe only c_t(x_t); decisions use previous plays, observed values and private randomness. Regret is E[sum_t c_t(x_t)]−min_{x∈S}sum_t c_t(x).
necessary_context.name: Online bandit model and regret

necessary_context.content: B is the Euclidean unit ball and the sphere is its boundary. The convex feasible set satisfies rB⊆S⊆RB, with positive radii. P_S is nearest-point Euclidean projection. L-Lipschitz means |f(x)−f(y)|≤L||x−y|| on the domain. Records explicitly select closed S so the projection and hindsight minimum are attained; this is an explicit well-posedness restriction, not a quotation of an additional printed assumption.
necessary_context.name: Geometry and access

necessary_context.content: hat f_delta(x)=E_{v uniform on B} f(x+delta v). The gradient estimator samples u uniformly on the unit sphere instead of the ball. The locally Lipschitz regularity restriction and its complete local justification are explicitly separated from the source's terse Lemma 1.
necessary_context.name: Ball smoothing versus sphere sampling
